quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 (DART half-year report, consolidated, reviewed by Samduk Accounting Corp.): revenue KRW 233,608M, +54.3% YoY against KRW 151,363M, but still an operating loss of KRW 12,329M (gross loss KRW 4,197M) because the Philippine plant ran at a loss; Q2 alone revenue KRW 126,288M against KRW 76,104M a year earlier. On a separate (parent-only) basis H1 revenue was KRW 230,892M with operating profit KRW 2,600M - revenue +57.0% YoY and a swing back into operating profit. Product mix: memory packages KRW 194,636M (83.3% of sales), non-memory packages KRW 38,518M (16.5%); domestic sales KRW 172,658M, exports KRW 60,950M.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 rev KRW 233,608M (+54.3% YoY); H1 operating loss KRW 12,329M; Q2 rev KRW 126,288M; separate-basis H1 rev KRW 230,892M with OP KRW 2,600M (+57.0%); memory 83.3% / non-memory 16.5%

quarterly_data.signal: Customer concentration and standing contracts (DART half-year report, as of 2026-06-30): the single largest customer, disclosed only as 'Company A', accounted for KRW 176,006M of H1 2026 revenue, up from KRW 96,272M in H1 2025; every line of the sales-channel table is sold to 'Samsung Electronics and others'. Disclosed auto-renewing supply agreements: Samsung Electronics for BOC-type packages (1999-01), basic production/assembly/test transaction agreements (2001-09 and 2019-07), S-LSI assembly and test (2004-09) and semiconductor bump/EDS work (2016-02); SK Hynix for 48TSOP and other contracted packages (2001-09); MXIC (2005-06); Fujitsu for FBGA (2010-02). The company states it supplies advanced packaging solutions to Samsung Electronics, Micron and IDT. No order backlog is managed - customer volumes are received daily and weekly and convert to revenue within 3 to 15 days.
quarterly_data.figure: Largest customer KRW 176,006M of H1 revenue (vs KRW 96,272M in H1 2025); no order backlog - orders convert to revenue in 3-15 days

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and utilisation H1 2026 (DART half-year report): package capacity 978M units (SFA Semiconductor Cheonan 175M, SFA Semicon Philippines 802M) against actual output of 590M units (Korea 70M, Philippines 520M) - average utilisation 60%, Korea 40% and Philippines 65%. Daily capacity is 0.97M packages in Korea and 4.46M in the Philippines over 30 operating days a month. The 2026 investment plan is KRW 15,700M of buildings and equipment to raise capacity (SFA Semiconductor KRW 13,100M, SFA Semicon Philippines KRW 2,600M), of which KRW 7,147M was spent in H1 and KRW 8,553M remains; property, plant and equipment additions were KRW 37,978M gross in H1 and contractual commitments to acquire PP&E stood at KRW 7,190,991 thousand.
quarterly_data.figure: Capacity 978M packages in H1, output 590M, utilisation 60% (Korea 40% / Philippines 65%); 2026 capex plan KRW 15,700M (KRW 7,147M spent, KRW 8,553M remaining)

quarterly_data.signal: Raw-material purchases and named suppliers H1 2026 (DART half-year report): package substrate (PCB) purchases of KRW 85,750M were 90.3% of raw-material spend, bought from Simmtech, Daeduck Electronics, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Fast Print and Daisho Denshi; gold wire KRW 7,333M (7.7%) from LT Metal and MK Electron; solder ball KRW 1,030M (1.1%) from MK Electron and Duksan Hi-Metal; EMC moulding compound KRW 895M (0.9%) from Samsung SDI, Hitachi, Nepes and KCC. The average PCB input price rose to KRW 822 from KRW 447 in FY2025 on a richer high-end substrate mix and a weaker won, and gold wire rose to KRW 272 from KRW 206 on the LME gold price - substrate and gold are the cost items inflating this OSAT's bill of materials.

quarterly_data.signal: R&D and product pipeline (DART half-year report): H1 R&D spend KRW 1,519M, 0.65% of revenue. Completed developments include fine-pitch Cu pillar bump packages, ELK (extreme low-k) flip-chip mass-production infrastructure with several new product wins, flip-chip flux jetting and SDTT wafer dicing. The forward programme targets large-body FCBGA (85 x 85), high-density large-area FCBGA no-pressure low-warpage bonding (national consortium project), laser-assist bonding, land-side capacitor attach, large-die thermal-compression flip-chip attach, fine-pitch Cu pillar and thick-RDL WLCSP, GaN and SiC wafer bumping, high-voltage power fine-pitch flip-chip bumping (national consortium project) and a glass-composite large-area multilayer wiring package (national consortium project). Bumping, added as a new business in 2014, is described as the company's growth engine alongside a push from memory into system LSI.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D KRW 1,519M (0.65% of sales); pipeline: large-body FCBGA 85 x 85, glass-composite multilayer package, laser-assist bonding, GaN/SiC wafer bumping, thick-RDL WLCSP

quarterly_data.signal: Segment and geography H1 2026 (DART half-year report): the Korean parent booked KRW 228,973M of segment revenue with operating profit KRW 1,068M, while SFA Semicon Philippines booked KRW 4,634M of external segment revenue with an operating loss of KRW 13,397M; the Philippine subsidiary's own H1 revenue was KRW 158,981M (mostly intercompany) with a half-year net loss of KRW 11,270M. Sales by destination: home country KRW 192,853M, United States KRW 31,300M, South-East Asia KRW 8,504M, Japan KRW 39M. The parent bought KRW 67,731,828 thousand of subcontract work from the Philippine plant in H1 (KRW 32,569,957 thousand a year earlier) and lent it USD 20,000 thousand (KRW 29,961M at 4.6%, 2026-05-15 to 2029-05-14).
